reasoning: Set A follows the user's brief more closely and is the stronger quant plan. Its M1 is a real walking skeleton: it runs a synthetic snapshot through qdata, qops, server and cockpit into the browser, with one parallel interface task per package. Stage 2 is judged out of sample on realized variance, against 1/N and sample minimum variance. It has known-answer benches, including published HRP and minimum-variance weights, for every estimator. Every feature, forecast and agent claim goes to the null-hypothesis-testing skill, with a calibrated within-date shuffle null and a deflated Sharpe ratio over a permanent model log. Forward paper trading is the deciding test. The ten test companies become a sourced golden case (TC-25), and the reference caveats are handled in the design (per-window refit, one scale, an embargo). Its weaknesses are size and some stale text. Over 130 KB of spec and architecture and 14 milestones make it heavy. Stage 4 is split into two stages, and the build order is awkward (M5 depends on M12). Workspace, AGENTS and CONSTRAINTS boundary lines still name only the Stage 1 packages, and TC-25's open question is stale. Set B is tighter and easier to read, with good held-out pre-registration and a claims ledger. But it splits Stage 1 by layer: M1 is backend only and M2 is app only. M2 to M8 have no Exit in the roadmap, M2's Depends cell omits the research milestones its views call, and no milestone depends on the real-data milestone M3. Stage 2 is scored on Sharpe instead of realized variance. A member-only Panel conflicts with holding names after they leave the index. Set B also defers the user's ten test companies, has no planted check for PPO and no forward paper trading, and leaves several 'no contract section yet' notes that are now false.
